questions.question: Which spec should we design first?

options.label: Stream lifecycle (Recommended)
options.description: Highest risk (time, ownership, closing), and nothing covers it yet. Gives the TLA+ pattern for 6 and 8.

options.label: Read contract
options.description: Smallest step from 051 (a single instant, pre/post only). Fast, but leaves the hard part for later.

options.label: Key admission
options.description: Settles the normalization question first. Narrow, pure function, Dafny-friendly.

questions.question: Key admission: normalize or reject non-canonical input?

options.label: Reject (Recommended)
options.description: One spelling per Key, consistent with 051's exact name equality. Callers get an error for `a//b` or `./a`.

options.label: Normalize a fixed set
options.description: Friendlier for callers, but every rewrite rule creates an alias that must be proved not to merge distinct Keys.

options.label: Decide later
options.description: Mark it an open question in the admission spec and keep it out of the other specs.

Second close() on an already Closed stream?

options.label: No-op (Recommended)
options.description: Matches Python's IO convention and makes `with` blocks plus explicit close safe. SL-006 still holds: no second release.

options.label: Raise
options.description: Surfaces double-close bugs in caller code, but breaks common Python idioms.

questions.question: What happens to open streams when their session (or the store) closes?

options.label: Streams fault (Recommended)
options.description: SL-009 as drafted: defined outcome, caller still closes. No orphan reads on a dead connection.

options.label: Session waits
options.description: Session close blocks until every stream is closed. Strong ownership, but one leaked stream hangs shutdown.

options.label: Streams keep working
options.description: Each stream holds its own connection. Simple for callers, but session close no longer bounds resource use.
